correctness.rationale: Full normal form for automorphisms follows from the characteristic derived ideal; invertibility of the fixed-point operator factors as (multiplier minus one) times det(A-I). Split orthogonal similitudes are precisely diagonal or anti-diagonal and yield 2(q-2)^2 admissible matrices. Non-split similitudes are the two norm-similitude cosets of F_{q^2}^× and yield 2(q+1)(q-2). Independent direct matrix enumerations over F3, F5, F7 agree. An explicit isotopism uses the invertible Gram-matrix transfer; nonisomorphism follows from unequal Witt indices. All finite fields of odd prime power q are covered by the proof, not merely the computations.

value.rationale: La Rosa–Mancini–Nagy isotopism deliberately identifies many nonisomorphic one-dimensional-derived nilpotent Leibniz algebras. The theorem exhibits a sharp structural limitation of this identification: the natural proportion of automorphisms with no nonzero fixed vector changes by an explicit nontrivial factor between the split and nonsplit members, for every odd finite field. This concrete all-field counterexample concerns invariance under algebra isotopism, not a routine isolated group order.
